metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully changed Chrome profile name from 'Person 1' to 'Thomas' by opening the profile menu, clicking Customise profile, selecting all text in the name field, and typing the new name.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome profile dropdown, navigate to Customise profile page, select and replace text in the name field.
metadata.explanation: Same profile-rename operation as source task but targeting name 'Alex' instead of 'Thomas'. Evaluator reads profile.name from Chrome preferences after restarting Chrome to flush state to disk.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter `get_profile_name` correctly reads `profile.name` from Chrome's Preferences file — exactly the state needed to verify a profile rename.
Metric `exact_match` correctly accesses `rules['expected']` (= 'Alex') and compares it against the extracted profile name with strict equality — correct parameter handling for `expected.type='rule'`.
Expected value 'Alex' exactly matches the instruction target name.
Postconfig kills Chrome (SIGTERM via pkill) before reading the preferences file, ensuring the in-memory state is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.
Single-objective task (rename profile to 'Alex') is fully covered by the single evaluator check.
Initial state ('Person 1') will not pass the exact_match check, providing negative-control resistance.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider adding a short sleep after `pkill chrome` (before relaunching) to ensure Chrome has fully written preferences before the relaunch reads the file — though in practice Chrome writes preferences periodically so this is unlikely to matter.
